messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High tail latency on streaming responses (svc=runtime, region=us-west-2). 3xx increase in p99 token time, error spike in push frames. auto-page: oncall (arjun)
maya: seeing >500ms p99 for /v1/stream and backlog growth on muxers, connections piling in ingress LB. starting investigation.
arjun: I'm on call. tagging eng-runtime and support. paging liam + eva. can we gate streaming quickly?
liam: quick check — kernel queues are saturated on the streaming worker pool, KV cache miss ratio spiked with long latencies. suspect batching pressure + a bad client burst.
eva: support reports two enterprise customers saw retries and some clients reported stuck SSE connections. no 5xx yet but many stalled.
maya: mitigation plan proposal: 1) flip streaming feature flag to off for public tenants (global kill-switch) 2) enable polling fallback with increased short-lived polling quota for affected customers 3) apply temporary ingress rate limit on /v1/stream to 5 rps per API key and reduce max concurrent frames.
arjun: agree. we'll do staged: canary us-west-2 -> region rollback -> global off. who will flip flags and coordinate comms?
liam: I'll flip the flag in the control plane and push a canary to us-west-2 now. command: 
```
# control-plane toggle
redwoodctl feature set streaming_responses false --scope region:us-west-2 --reason "emergency latency mitigation"
```
liam: doing it in 30s, will monitor metrics.
maya: set oncall channel to notice and create alert to watch for connection drop count.
oncall-pager: arjun acknowledged the pager.
arjun: liam go for it. eva prep status note for affected customers: brief + workaround (use polling endpoint /v1/poll with 3s poll).
eva: drafting support message: "We observed elevated latency for streaming responses and are temporarily disabling real-time streaming. Clients should switch to our polling endpoint /v1/poll for uninterrupted responses. We'll update when streaming is restored." sending to Natalie for product sign-off.
natalie: OK approve. add estimated ETA: 30-45m and mention root-cause investigation continuing. Also include recommendations for SDK team to roll client-side exponential backoff.
liam: flag toggled in us-west-2. metrics: p99 down from 520ms -> 120ms in canary within 90s. ingress queue length reduced.
maya: good. proceed global after 10m observation if stable.
liam: rolling global toggle in progress. command: 
```
redwoodctl feature set streaming_responses false --scope global --reason "emergency: stabilize throughput"
```
liam: global toggle complete. verifying.
arjun: confirm we also applied temporary quota bump on polling for affected customers: 
```
# quota bump
redwoodctl quota adjust --endpoint /v1/poll --customer enterprise-123 --delta +200r/min --ttl 60m
```
maya: applied global ingress rate-limit on /v1/stream: 5 rps default, 2 concurrent frames, and traffic shaping rule to route excess to polling.
eva: support message posted to affected customers and status.redwood.com incident created.
oncall-pager: incident assigned to arjun; escalation policy running to eng-runtime.
arjun: initial impact: ~120 customer connections switched automatically to polling, 3 customers required manual SDK change (we contacted them). No major revenue impact detected so far.
liam: logs showing suppressed push errors after the toggle: 
```
[2026-03-17T19:15:02Z] svc=runtime worker=stream-7 latency_p99=118ms backlog=12
[2026-03-17T19:16:10Z] svc=runtime worker=stream-3 frames_dropped=0 connections_closed=8
```
maya: good signals. action items: (1) keep streaming disabled until we fix batching/queue handling and validate under load (2) implement per-client smoothing + client-id fair-queueing (liam/eng-runtime) (3) add better consumer-side SDK fallback docs (natalie/devex) (4) post-mortem & RCA (arjun).
arjun: logging the incident and assigning PM/Eng leads. ETA for restore: target 24-48h after fixes and canary validation. For now leave feature OFF and monitor.
liam: creating a short-term task to add a softer degrade mode (emit truncated responses instead of blocking) and experiment with KV cache tuning.
eva: support to follow up with customers during morning. will collect any escalations.
natalie: will coordinate coms + status updates. plan: update status page in 30m and then hourly.
maya: closing thread for live ops. if any regression or customer adverse events, ping #pager immediately. great job team. :thumbsup:
